discovery_articles.title: Zantigo in St Paul, Minnesota
discovery_articles.snippet: In the vast graveyard of fast food chains, sometimes there is a resurrection. Founded in Minneapolis 7 years after Taco Bell, Zantigo (named Zapato at that time) had a similar model of rearranging the same array of a few ingredients to fill out a menu of Mexican-American dishes. After growing to 82 restaurants by 1986, Zantigo's parent company merged with it's rival's and within 2 years, all remaining Zantigo locations had been closed or converted to Taco Bells.

discovery_articles.title: The Old Place at Sam Houston Park in Houston, Texas
discovery_articles.snippet: At the edge of downtown lies Sam Houston Park, a manicured green haven that doubles as a time capsule. While the park is home to the Houston Heritage Society Museum which includes several historic structures, none are older, or more resilient, than a humble, rough-hewn log structure known simply as The Old Place. Constructed around 1823, this cedar cabin is widely believed to be the oldest remaining structure in Harris County.

featured_read.title: What Makes You You Makes the Universe: Nobel Laureate Erwin Schrödinger on Quantum Physics, Vedanta, and the Ongoing Mystery of What We Are
featured_read.snippet: "This life of yours which you are living is not merely a piece of the entire existence, but is in a certain sense the whole."
featured_read.blurb: Schrödinger — the man who gave us the cat — spent his later years arguing, through quantum physics and ancient Vedantic philosophy, that individual consciousness isn't a fragment of the universe but somehow the whole thing, looking at itself. It's the kind of idea that sounds mystical until the math starts to agree with it.

garden_note.note: The evening air in Zürich carries that particular late-summer weight — warm and faintly dusty, with the sunflowers leaning gold against a sky that doesn't fully surrender until well past nine. This is the quiet pivot point of the season, when the garden asks you to harvest a little more urgently than you planted.

fern_data.greeting: A day ends the way most do — not with a bang but with the quiet accumulation of everything you half-noticed. Tonight there's Nero to reconsider, a Phoebe Bridgers record that earns the word 'masterwork,' and Schrödinger asking what you actually are — which feels, honestly, like the right question for this hour.
